name: Notification Idempotency Map
purpose: Document notification idempotency mechanisms to ensure exactly-once delivery semantics where required

idempotency_mechanisms.description: Stores notification metadata with unique identifiers to prevent duplicate processing
implementation_details: notification_logs table with columns: id, notification_type, recipient_id, external_reference, sent_at, status
Before sending notification, check if record exists with same notification_type, recipient_id, and external_reference
If record exists and status is 'sent', skip sending
If record exists and status is 'failed', may retry based on retry policy

examples.example: Booking confirmation emails deduplicated by booking ID
Payment receipt emails deduplicated by payment ID

idempotency_mechanisms.description: Leverages external service built-in idempotency mechanisms
implementation_details: Generate unique idempotency key for each notification request
Send idempotency key to external service in request headers
External service ignores requests with duplicate idempotency keys
Key typically based on business entity ID + timestamp or UUID

examples.example: Payment requests use payment_id as idempotency key
SMS requests use randomly generated UUID

weaknesses: Only works for external services that support it
No persistence of sent notifications in application

idempotency_mechanisms.description: Queue system prevents duplicate job processing
implementation_details: Before queuing job, check for recent similar jobs in queue
If similar job exists and is pending/processing, skip queuing
Implementation varies by queue system (Redis, database, etc.)
Often based on job class and payload hash
weaknesses: Doesn't prevent duplicates if job already processed

idempotency_mechanisms.description: In-memory cache to prevent duplicate notifications within request lifecycle
implementation_details: Checked before attempting to send notification
idempotency_mechanisms.technology: PHP static variables or request-scoped services

examples.purpose: Prevent duplicate emails within same web request
examples.example: Controller and observer both trying to send same notification

details.notes: Email via NotificationService (db-backed), queued SendEmailJob (job dedup)
Stored directly in database, duplicates possible if triggered multiple times

summary.coverage: High for email notifications, variable for other types
recommendations: Standardize on database-backed deduplication for all critical notifications
Ensure queued notifications use job deduplication
Leverage external service idempotency keys where available
Remove application-cache-only mechanisms for notifications requiring durability
Consider implementing a notification outbox pattern for guaranteed delivery
